newsitem.title: GERMANY: Two German insurers agree to mega-merger.
newsitem.headline: Two German insurers agree to mega-merger.

text.p: German insurance companies Victoria Holding AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer AG on Thursday signed a declaration of intent to merge to form the second largest insurer in Germany behind Allianz AG, Victoria said.
The new company will be called ERGO Versicherungsgruppe and will be based in Duesseldorf, Victoria said in a mandatory statement released late on Thursday night.
Reinsurance group Munich Re, which owns 80 percent of Hamburg-Mannheimer as well as a minority stake in Victoria Holding, will have a majority stake in the holding company of the new group.

Munich Re said in a separate statement that it supported the merger. Based on the accounts of the year 1996 alone, the link-up will result in an increase of around five marks in Munich Re's earnings per share.
"The ERGO group will be excellently positioned in the German insurance market, the third largest in the world, with a good base for expanding business in the rest of Europe," Victoria said.
The inclusion of Victoria in Munich Re's group of consolidated companies will boost Munich Re's consolidated premium income by some 8.4 billion marks to about 46.6 billion marks, Munich Re said.
Victoria Holding offers all the main lines of life and non-life insurance and owns D.A.S. Allgemeine Rechtsschutz-Versicherungs-AG, Europe's largest legal protection insurer, Victoria said.

The Hamburg-Mannheimer group, the second largest life insurer and the second largest personal accident insurer in Germany, also includes DKV Deutsche Krankenverischerung AG, Europe's largest private health insurer.
"It is envisaged that the group's business will focus primarily on personal lines insurance and commercial cover for small and medium-sized businesses," Victoria said.
"With premium income of around 21 billion marks, it will occupy second place in the German insurance market."

Before the merger is effected, the stakes held by Hamburg-Mannheimer AG in the share capital of DKV Deutsche Krankenversicherung AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer Sachversicherungs-AG, currently amounting to nearly 40 percent each, are both to be increased to around 100 percent through capital increases in return for stock.
The individual insurers will continue to operate with their established brand names, Victoria said.
The merger is has yet to be approved by the Federal Cartel Office and the shareholders of Victoria Holding AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer AG.
